- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 75+), overshooting by 2–5% in next 3–5 days; apply dampening factor to peak forecasts.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often misses early downward trends; shift forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (no strong sentiment), model tends to drift toward historical mean; anchor forecast to 30-day moving average of prior 10–15 days.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves after recent lows unless sentiment is > 0.67; model overestimates momentum in such cases.
